claims.explanation: evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:5-9 reports baseline/reference losses and scores, but C01 independently asserts the log(loss-1.5) transformation and approximately 0.68 additive score-unit improvement. The reported-evidence catalog supports cell ordering and ratios, not this logarithmic identity or additive magnitude. Declaring only reference < baseline would discard conditions. The table also reports reference score 1.143 whereas the claim uses approximately 1.13; neither value was rewritten.

evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:13-21 gives the analytical formula and halving argument. C02 asserts an asymptote and the universal identity that halving loss-1.5 changes score by -log(2), not an ordering among reported cells. No installed relation expresses that functional identity and domain limit; finite reruns would not discharge the mathematical assertion.

The C03 heading says unigram is worse, while its Statement and src/kernel/notes.md:3,18-19 say loss 7.58 is marginally below the 7.636 MLP baseline. evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:27-29 records scores 1.814 and 1.808. The fixed inputs do not resolve the direction conflict. The additional assertion that both round to approximately 1.81 would also require a rounding/equality relation, not just a loss comparison.

C04 simultaneously says bigrams beat every neural-only attempt and describes losses 5.83/5.75 as better than conv-only loss 5.25, while qualifying conv as a later experiment. src/kernel/notes.md:5-7 and evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:30-32 retain those losses; logic/experiments.md E03-E04 says conv beats bigrams. The required historical neural-only cohort and temporal comparison are not specified consistently, so no scope or comparator was guessed.

src/kernel/notes.md:7 and evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:32 report Conv1D loss 5.25; the claim requires that attained loss for kernel=7, hidden=512, layers=6, expansion=2 after 100k steps, not merely a lower loss than bigrams. No reported-evidence relation tests a cell against an absolute target. src/kernel/tao_train.py:19,24-30,73-75 configures these hyperparameters for the shipped composite, not a separately logged ConvMLM-only run, so training-condition attribution cannot be strengthened.

evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:32-33 and src/kernel/notes.md:7,11 give the 5.25 to 4.6 loss change. src/kernel/tao_solution.py:332-359 identifies the learned scalar initialized to 1.0 and frozen bigram path. A comparative property could express lower composite loss, but would not preserve the claimed endpoint magnitudes or largest-single-win assertion, which needs comparisons of stage-to-stage differences. The catalog has no reported difference-of-differences or attained-value relation.

src/kernel/tao_solution.py:293-297,346,363-367 and src/kernel/tao_train.py:123 locate multiplication by inverse_stds in forward and reciprocal EMA updates in the training loop. C07 is a code-location/primitive-compliance mechanism assertion. Numeric cell relations do not establish where division occurs or whether the forward-pass restriction is obeyed.

src/kernel/tao_solution.py:206-236 implements padding, an as_strided view and einsum, with pad=(kernel_size-1)//2. C08 asserts an implementation substitution and preserved same-padding behavior under the primitive allow-list, not a reported quantitative comparison. No catalog relation expresses code construction or allow-list membership.

src/kernel/notes.md:13-16 contains the approximation MFU measurements, the approximately 23x slowdown, and the observation that loss did not decrease. evidence/tables/reference_scores.md:34 instead marks the approximation loss/score n/a. There is no parseable matched runtime and learning-curve evidence covering both the slowdown and failed training conjuncts. The notes distinguish GPT-2-small's 2.3 MFU from a smaller configuration's 1.88 versus 43.9 MFU; those variants were not merged.

evidence/tables/human_baselines.md:5-27 supplies all 11 scores and summary rows. C10 additionally asserts best-loss inversion, an approximately 0.79 additive score gap, median 1.36354 and exactly five worse-than-anchor humans. Reported cell comparisons cannot express the logarithmic inversion, median calculation or exact additive magnitude; retaining only selected humans beating reference would narrow the claim. The evidence's four beat-reference humans and its stated 1.13 anchor were preserved, not reconciled with the claim's count.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md:13-36,40-48,64-67 records 22 runs, their model identities, the two named winning scores and the Sonnet best. The whole claim also requires run_14 to be within 0.09 score-units of the reference and the named attained scores. The catalog's comparisons/count-at-least scans cannot preserve this absolute-distance and attained-value conjunction. In particular run_14's reported 1.2218 and the prose reference 1.13 were not adjusted to make the stated 0.09 condition true.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md:40-46,64-70 provides median/mean best-of-run and per-model mean values, while evidence/tables/human_baselines.md:23 supplies the best human. C12 asserts those attained aggregates, approximately 0.6 above reference, the 0.71 best-human gap and the 0.247 Opus-versus-Sonnet mean gap. No reported-evidence relation checks these median/mean identities and additive differences; simple model ordering would not be the same obligation.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md:58-60,76-77 and logic/experiments.md EM01-EM04 describe ReLU-attention winners, no loaded bigram priors across 22 runs and the three-seed ensemble. C13 combines those code-history assertions with a learning-rate ceiling and an asserted 0.55-loss-unit official contribution; a score comparison or count relation would not establish the whole conjunction. The per-run code/rebench-pipeline paths cited by C13 are not part of this copied ARA, and the official table's 5.25 to 4.6 change was not changed to match 0.55.

evidence/tables/malt_attempts.md:74-77 names runs 01,06,09,11,16,19,20 and narrates NaNs and recovery by fixed residual scaling; logic/experiments.md EM05 summarizes seven of 22. C14 requires universal recovery across those cases, timing at or shortly after step zero, the reciprocal-emulation cause, and absence of the official workaround. The table has no per-step failure/recovery measurements, and numeric cell relations do not express this causal/code-history conjunction. The cited external per-run insights are unavailable within the fixed copy.
